unit.label: Routines, food & dinner plans
unit.title: Routines & Common Ground
unit.description: 7 new words and expressions. Talk about morning and evening routines, choose Vietnamese food for dinner, and explain what your group does or does not share.

goal.text: 我們晚上一起吃晚飯，好不好？
goal.pinyin: Wǒmen wǎnshàng yìqǐ chī wǎnfàn, hǎo bu hǎo?
goal.meaning: How about we eat dinner together this evening?

unit.bookReference: A Course in Contemporary Chinese 1 · Lesson 3 週末做什麼？ · vocabulary pp. 46, 48–49; topic sentences and adverb order pp. 52–55; suggestion practice p. 59

lessons.title: Morning Routines
lessons.subtitle: Learn 早上, then add a matching whole group.

steps.prompt: Which order means “They all also like swimming in the morning”?
options: 他們也都喜歡早上游泳。
他們都也喜歡早上游泳。
他們早上游泳也都喜歡。
steps.answer: 他們也都喜歡早上游泳。
steps.explanation: Use group + 也 + 都 + preference. 早上 stays with the swimming activity.

lessons.title: Evening Habits
lessons.subtitle: Learn 晚上 and layer 都, 常, and 也.

steps.prompt: Which time phrase means “tomorrow evening”?
steps.explanation: Chinese orders the larger time before the smaller time: 明天 + 晚上.

steps.prompt: In 他們晚上也都常看電影, what does each adverb contribute?
options: 也 adds a match; 都 includes everyone; 常 marks frequency
也 marks frequency; 都 means evening; 常 adds a match
All three mean exactly the same thing
steps.answer: 也 adds a match; 都 includes everyone; 常 marks frequency
steps.explanation: Read from the action outward: 常看電影, 都常看電影, 也都常看電影.

steps.prompt: Which sentence has the natural adverb order?
options: 他們晚上也都常看電影。
他們晚上都也常看電影。
他們晚上常也都看電影。
steps.answer: 他們晚上也都常看電影。
steps.explanation: With all three, use 也 + 都 + 常 before the action.

lessons.title: Eat Dinner Together
lessons.subtitle: Learn 吃晚飯 and place time or togetherness before the action.

steps.prompt: Which phrase means “eat dinner”?
steps.explanation: 吃 is the action and 晚飯 is the meal: 吃晚飯.

lessons.title: Food & Group Preferences
lessons.subtitle: Learn 菜, then say what nobody wants or has.

steps.prompt: Nobody in the group wants dinner. Which sentence states that precisely?
steps.explanation: 都不 applies the negative to every member of the group.

steps.prompt: Which means “None of us has an older brother”?
steps.explanation: 都 refers to all of 我們; 沒有 is the negative of 有.

lessons.title: Vietnamese Food for Dinner
lessons.subtitle: Learn 越南, then distinguish nobody from not everybody.

steps.prompt: Two people want Vietnamese food; one does not. Which sentence describes the group?
steps.explanation: The preference is not shared by everyone: 不都.

steps.prompt: Nobody wants Vietnamese food. Which sentence states the strongest, exact claim “none”?
steps.explanation: 都不 explicitly says nobody wants it. 不都 says only “not all,” so it does not express the full information.

steps.prompt: You want Vietnamese food. Which reply says that?
steps.explanation: 越南 is the country; 越南菜 is its cuisine. 吃越南菜 says to eat the food.

lessons.title: Make a Plan Together
lessons.subtitle: Agree on the time, choose the food, and check the plan.

steps.prompt: What is 好不好 doing at the end of the dinner sentence?
options: Asking whether the suggestion sounds good
steps.answer: Asking whether the suggestion sounds good
steps.explanation: After a proposed plan, 好不好 checks whether the other person agrees.

steps.prompt: The plan is 明天晚上. When are you meeting?
steps.explanation: 明天 gives the day and 晚上 narrows it to the evening.

steps.prompt: Your friends say 我們都不想吃越南菜. What have you learned?
options: Nobody in this group wants Vietnamese food
Only one person dislikes the food
steps.answer: Nobody in this group wants Vietnamese food
steps.explanation: The negative is about wanting 越南菜. It does not say the group wants no dinner at all.

steps.prompt: You want to suggest eating Vietnamese food together tomorrow evening. Which plan includes all those details?
options: 我們明天晚上一起去吃越南菜，好不好？
我們明天早上一起去吃越南菜，好不好？
我們明天晚上一起去游泳，好不好？
steps.answer: 我們明天晚上一起去吃越南菜，好不好？
steps.explanation: Check the time, the shared activity, and the food before asking 好不好.

steps.prompt: Which reply naturally accepts 我們晚上一起吃晚飯，好不好？
steps.explanation: 好啊 is a natural acceptance of the suggestion.

steps.prompt: A friend proposes dinner this evening. You want tomorrow evening instead. Which reply offers that alternative?
options: 我們明天晚上一起吃晚飯，好不好？
我們今天晚上一起吃晚飯，好不好？
我們明天早上一起去游泳，好不好？
steps.answer: 我們明天晚上一起吃晚飯，好不好？
steps.explanation: Keep the dinner plan and change the time to 明天晚上.

lessons.title: Unit Challenge
lessons.subtitle: Use every Unit 10 word and structure without new material.

steps.prompt: Which time phrase means “tomorrow morning”?
steps.explanation: Use larger-to-smaller time order.

steps.prompt: Which activity means “eat dinner”?
steps.explanation: 吃 is “eat” and 晚飯 is “dinner.”

steps.prompt: Choose the natural “also all often” order.
steps.explanation: Build in the learned order: 也 + 都 + 常.

steps.prompt: Complete: 我沒有哥哥，___姐姐。
steps.explanation: Keep 也 before 沒有.

steps.prompt: Nobody likes swimming. Which statement explicitly says “none of them,” giving the strongest information?
steps.explanation: 都不 explicitly states that nobody likes it. 不都 only denies that everyone likes it and is less informative.

steps.prompt: Three people: ✅ · ❌ · ✅. Which statement fits?
steps.explanation: 不都 means “not all,” so a mixed group fits.

steps.prompt: What does 好不好 ask after a complete plan?
steps.explanation: It checks a suggestion after the plan is stated.

steps.prompt: What does 越南菜 mean?
options: An evening meal of any kind
steps.explanation: 越南 is Vietnam; adding 菜 names its cuisine.

steps.prompt: Which final exchange is natural and matches the meaning?
options: A：我們晚上一起吃晚飯，好不好？ B：好啊！
A：我們晚上一起吃晚飯，好不好？ B：我沒有哥哥。
A：我們晚上一起吃晚飯，好不好？ B：他們不都游泳。
steps.answer: A：我們晚上一起吃晚飯，好不好？ B：好啊！
steps.explanation: 好不好 asks for agreement; 好啊 naturally accepts.

newVocabulary.note: A time word. Put it before the action or habit it frames.
A time word used before the action or habit it frames.

newVocabulary.meaning: how about it?; does that sound good?
newVocabulary.note: Place it after a suggestion to ask whether the other person agrees.
Use it after a country name to name a cuisine.
越南菜 means Vietnamese food. Learn the country name as one word.

早.note: 早 begins 早上, morning. Notice 日 above 十.
早.memory: 早 stacks a compact 日 over 十. The last vertical passes through the lower horizontal, not through the box above it.

parts.label: 日
parts.name: upper box
parts.description: The first four strokes form 日. Keep this box centered above the lower crossing strokes.

parts.label: 十
parts.name: lower cross
parts.description: Write the broad horizontal below 日, then the vertical through that horizontal to complete 十.

上.meaning: final syllable in 早上 and 晚上
上.note: 早上 (zǎoshàng) means morning. 上 has a vertical, a short horizontal to its right, and a long base line. The small bar sits above the base, which helps distinguish 上 from 下.
上.memory: 上 has a vertical, a short horizontal to its right, and a long base line. The small bar sits above the base, which helps distinguish 上 from 下.

parts.label: 上
parts.name: 上 component
parts.description: Begin with the vertical, add the short bar to its right, and finish with the long horizontal base. Keep the short bar above that base.

晚.note: 晚 appears in 晚上, evening, and 晚飯, dinner.
晚.memory: 晚 has 日 on the left and 免 on the right. The right side begins with a small slant and bend above a box, then spreads into two lower strokes.

parts.label: 日
parts.name: sun-shaped left side
parts.description: The four strokes of 日 make a compact box at the left. Keep enough space for the wider 免 on the right.

parts.label: 免
parts.name: right-hand component
parts.description: The seven strokes of 免 include an upper slant and bend, a box-like middle, and two spreading lower strokes.

吃.note: 吃晚飯 (chī wǎnfàn) means eat dinner. 吃 puts 口 beside 乞. The right side has a short slant and horizontal above a bent hook; do not add an extra horizontal to 乞.
吃.memory: 吃 puts 口 beside 乞. The right side has a short slant and horizontal above a bent hook; keep 乞 to three clear strokes without an extra horizontal.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: 口 component
parts.description: The first three strokes make the mouth-shaped box on the left. A mouth is a useful meaning clue for eating.

parts.label: 乞
parts.name: 乞 component
parts.description: The right side has three strokes: a short slant, a short horizontal, then a long bent hook below them.

飯.note: 飯 completes 晚飯, dinner. The food component is the Traditional form 飠.
飯.memory: 飯 places the narrow food component 飠 beside 反. The right side starts with a sloping cover above two crossing lower strokes.

parts.label: 飠
parts.name: food component
parts.description: The first eight strokes form the food component on the left, a useful meaning clue for a meal.

parts.label: 反
parts.name: right-hand component
parts.description: 反 uses four strokes on the right: two upper sloping strokes above the crossing lower strokes of 又.

菜.note: 菜 can refer to dishes or a style of cooking. Here it names a cuisine after a country name.
菜.memory: 菜 has the grass top 艹 above 采. In this Taiwan form, the grass top uses four strokes; below it, a claw-like top sits over 木.

parts.label: 艹
parts.name: grass top
parts.description: Write the four short strokes across the top in two groups. This plant-related component gives a useful clue to the food meaning.

parts.label: 采
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: The next four strokes form the claw-like top of 采, and the last four form 木 below. Keep 采 centered under 艹.

越.meaning: first syllable of 越南, Vietnam
越.note: In this unit, learn 越 as part of the country name 越南. It is not a new comparison pattern.
越.memory: 走 runs down the left and stretches underneath 戉 on the right. The long lower stroke supports the right-hand component.

parts.label: 走
parts.name: walking component
parts.description: These seven strokes form 走, with 土 above the lower strokes. Its long final stroke extends under the right side.

parts.label: 戉
parts.name: right-hand component
parts.description: Five strokes form 戉. Notice its bent strokes, long diagonal hook, and final small mark at the upper right.

南.meaning: final syllable of 越南, Vietnam
南.note: 南 completes 越南, Vietnam. The country name is pronounced Yuènán, with fourth tone then second tone.
南.memory: 南 begins with 十. Beneath it, an open-bottom frame surrounds two short marks and the lower crossing strokes.

parts.label: 十
parts.name: top cross
parts.description: The horizontal and vertical form a cross above the wide lower frame.

parts.label: 冂
parts.name: outer frame
parts.description: The left vertical and the top-right hooked stroke make the frame, open at its base.

parts.label: 𢆉
parts.name: inner strokes
parts.description: Two short inward marks sit above two horizontal strokes. Finish with the central vertical through those horizontals.

u10-also-all.title: Another whole group does too
u10-also-all.explanation: You already know 也 adds a matching fact and 都 includes everyone in a group. Now combine them. Build the meaning from the action outward: 喜歡游泳 = like swimming; 都喜歡游泳 = all like swimming; 也都喜歡游泳 = also all like swimming. The group comes first, then 也, then 都. Use 也 when the context supplies a matching fact, often in a previous statement. These sentences describe shared preferences; they do not say everyone swims together.

examples.text: 我喜歡游泳，他們也都喜歡游泳。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuān yóuyǒng, tāmen yě dōu xǐhuān yóuyǒng.
examples.meaning: I like swimming; all of them like swimming too.

examples.text: 我家人都喜歡照相，他家人也都喜歡照相。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiārén dōu xǐhuān zhàoxiàng, tā jiārén yě dōu xǐhuān zhàoxiàng.
examples.meaning: My family members all like taking photos; his family members all like taking photos too.

u10-also-all.remember: For “also all,” keep 也 before 都. 都 includes the members of the group before it; 也 connects this fact to another relevant fact.

u10-all-often.title: Everyone has the habit
u10-all-often.explanation: 常 tells how often an action happens. 都 tells who is included. Build outward: 看電影 = watch movies; 常看電影 = often watch movies; 都常看電影 = all often watch movies. In 我們都常看電影, each of us has this habit. The sentence does not say we watch together or at the same time. Keep 都 before 常 for this meaning.

examples.meaning: We all often watch movies.
They all often exercise.

u10-all-often.remember: Read the layers: everyone in the group → often → action. 都 is about the group; 常 is about frequency.

u10-also-all-often.title: That is our habit too
u10-also-all-often.pattern: group + 也 + 都 + 常 + activity
u10-also-all-often.explanation: Add 也 to a habit shared by every member of another group. Start with 喝茶, drink tea. 常喝茶 means often drink tea. 都常喝茶 means all often drink tea. 也都常喝茶 means also all often drink tea. So the practiced order is 也 → 都 → 常 → action. First establish the matching habit in the conversation; then add the group. You are combining familiar meanings, not learning a new word for “together.”

examples.text: 我常喝茶，他們也都常喝茶。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ cháng hē chá, tāmen yě dōu cháng hē chá.
examples.meaning: I often drink tea; all of them often drink tea too.

examples.text: 你常游泳，我們也都常游泳。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ cháng yóuyǒng, wǒmen yě dōu cháng yóuyǒng.
examples.meaning: You often swim; all of us often swim too.

u10-also-all-often.remember: 也 adds “too,” 都 includes everyone, and 常 adds “often.” We are practicing this order, not every possible adverb combination.

u10-also-no-have.title: I do not have one either
u10-also-no-have.explanation: You already use 沒有 for “do not have.” Put 也 before the whole negative: 也沒有 means “do not have … either.” You can add another person with the same situation, or another thing the same person does not have. In the second example, the second 我 is understood because the person has not changed. Keep 也 before 沒有. This lesson uses 沒有 only for having something, not as a new rule about past actions.

examples.text: 他沒有哥哥，我也沒有哥哥。
examples.pinyin: Tā méiyǒu gēge, wǒ yě méiyǒu gēge.
examples.meaning: He does not have an older brother; I do not have an older brother either.

examples.text: 我沒有哥哥，也沒有姐姐。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ méiyǒu gēge, yě méiyǒu jiějie.
examples.meaning: I do not have an older brother, and I do not have an older sister either.

u10-also-no-have.remember: Use 也不 with familiar verbs such as 喜歡. Use 也沒有 with 有: the negative of 有 is 沒有, never 不有.

u10-none.title: Nobody in the group
u10-none.explanation: To say a statement is false for every member of a group, put 都 before 不. Check one person at a time. For “likes swimming”: Person 1 ❌; Person 2 ❌; Person 3 ❌. Nobody in this group likes swimming. This is 都不喜歡游泳. The order is group → 都 → 不 → 喜歡游泳: for each person, “likes swimming” is not true. We are talking about this group, not everybody in the world. Compare the two examples below with the familiar positive pattern 都喜歡.

examples.meaning: None of us likes swimming. Likes swimming: Person 1 ❌ · Person 2 ❌ · Person 3 ❌.

examples.pinyin: Tāmen dōu bù xǐhuān hē kāfēi.
examples.meaning: None of them likes drinking coffee. Likes coffee: Person 1 ❌ · Person 2 ❌ · Person 3 ❌.

u10-none.remember: 都不 = none of the group satisfies the statement. A dislike does not tell you whether someone knows how to do the activity.

u10-none-have.title: Nobody has it; I have neither
u10-none-have.pattern: group or topic set + … + 都 + 沒有 + …
u10-none-have.explanation: 有 uses 沒有 as its negative. Add 都 before 沒有 to apply “do not have” to every member of a set. In 我們都沒有哥哥, 都 refers to us: no one in our group has an older brother. The set can also be the two topics you already learned to put first. In 哥哥、姐姐，我都沒有, it refers to older brothers and older sisters: I have neither. Read the words before 都 to find the set. Do not replace 沒有 with 不有.

examples.meaning: None of us has an older brother.
Older brothers and older sisters — I have neither.
None of them has an older sister.
Older brothers and older sisters — he has neither.

u10-none-have.remember: 都沒有 can mean “none of us has …” or “I have neither,” depending on the set before it. 沒有 stays together.

u10-not-all.title: Not everyone is the same
u10-not-all.explanation: 不都 rejects “all.” First imagine three people: Person 1 ✅ likes swimming; Person 2 ❌ does not; Person 3 ✅ likes swimming. 他們不都喜歡游泳 fits: not all of them like swimming. Contrast 都不: Person 1 ❌; Person 2 ❌; Person 3 ❌, so nobody likes it. 不都 does not tell us an exact number. At least one member does not fit the statement. In everyday group comparisons it often suggests a mixed group, like the picture here, but the words “not all” alone do not guarantee that anyone does fit. For an explicitly all-negative group, use 都不 to say “none” precisely.

examples.meaning: Not all of them like swimming. One possible group: Person 1 ✅ · Person 2 ❌ · Person 3 ✅.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bù dōu xǐhuān hē kāfēi.
examples.meaning: Not all of us like drinking coffee. One possible group: Person 1 ❌ · Person 2 ✅ · Person 3 ❌.

u10-not-all.remember: 都不: everyone → not; none. 不都: not → everyone; not all. The two orders make different claims and are not interchangeable.

u10-morning-time.title: Say when: 早上
u10-morning-time.pattern: (day) + 早上 + subject + action OR subject + 早上 + action
u10-morning-time.explanation: 早上 means “morning” or “in the morning.” Put the time before the action it frames. If you also name a day, Chinese normally goes from the larger time to the smaller time: 明天早上, “tomorrow morning.” A time phrase may come before the subject or just after it.

examples.meaning: I often drink tea in the morning.
Tomorrow morning, we are going swimming.

u10-morning-time.remember: Time comes before the action. For two time words, go from larger to smaller: 明天 → 早上.

u10-evening-time.title: Say when: 晚上
u10-evening-time.pattern: (day) + 晚上 + subject + action OR subject + 晚上 + action
u10-evening-time.explanation: 晚上 means “evening” or “at night.” Like 早上, it comes before the action it frames. With a day, keep the larger-to-smaller order: 明天晚上, “tomorrow evening.”

examples.meaning: I often watch movies in the evening.
We are watching a movie tomorrow evening.

u10-evening-time.remember: Put 晚上 before the action. With 明天, say 明天晚上—not 晚上明天.

u10-eat-dinner.title: Eat dinner
u10-eat-dinner.explanation: 吃 is the verb “to eat.” 晚飯 is dinner, the evening meal. Put the verb first: 吃晚飯. You can place a time such as 晚上 before this action.

examples.meaning: I eat dinner in the evening.
We eat dinner together.

u10-eat-dinner.remember: Action first, meal second: 吃 + 晚飯.

u10-how-about.title: Check a suggestion with 好不好
u10-how-about.explanation: After you suggest a plan, add 好不好？ to ask whether it sounds good to the other person. It literally presents “good or not good,” but the natural meaning here is “How about it?” or “Does that sound good?” Keep it at the end of the complete suggestion.

examples.text: 我們晚上一起吃晚飯，好不好？
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen wǎnshàng yìqǐ chī wǎnfàn, hǎo bu hǎo?
examples.meaning: How about we eat dinner together this evening?

examples.text: 我們明天早上去游泳，好不好？
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān zǎoshàng qù yóuyǒng, hǎo bu hǎo?
examples.meaning: How about we go swimming tomorrow morning?

u10-how-about.remember: Say the plan first, then ask 好不好？ for agreement.

u10-cuisine.title: Choose something to eat
u10-cuisine.pattern: 吃 + 菜; country name + 菜
u10-cuisine.explanation: 菜 can mean a dish or a cuisine. 吃菜 means to eat dishes or food. A country name before 菜 names that country’s cuisine; you will learn one in the next lesson. Keep the familiar order: person, time if needed, then 吃 and the food.

examples.meaning: We eat the dishes together.
I would like to eat some dishes this evening.

u10-cuisine.remember: 晚飯 names the meal. 菜 names dishes or a cuisine. Both follow 吃.

u10-vietnam.title: Vietnamese food
u10-vietnam.pattern: 越南 + 菜 → 越南菜
u10-vietnam.explanation: 越南, Yuènán, is Vietnam. Add the familiar 菜 to name its cuisine: 越南菜, Vietnamese food. This is a country name plus 菜, not a new verb. You can now say what kind of food you would like for dinner.

examples.meaning: I would like to eat Vietnamese food.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen wǎnshàng qù chī Yuènán cài.
examples.meaning: We are going to eat Vietnamese food this evening.

u10-vietnam.remember: 越南 = Vietnam; 越南菜 = Vietnamese food. Put 吃 before the food.

u10-review-both.note: Review: 都 includes everyone in 我們. This does not say we swim together.

u10-family-too.pinyin: Tā jiārén yě dōu xǐhuān zhàoxiàng.
u10-family-too.meaning: His family members all like taking photos too.
u10-family-too.note: Context: my family members all like taking photos. Add his family with 也都. Build 喜歡照相, then 都喜歡照相, then 也都喜歡照相.

u10-we-too.note: Context: someone else likes swimming. 也 adds our group; 都 includes each of us.

u10-they-music-too.pinyin: Tāmen yě dōu xǐhuān tīng yīnyuè.
u10-they-music-too.meaning: They all like listening to music too.
u10-they-music-too.note: Use this after a matching statement about someone else. Keep 也 before 都.

u10-review-often.note: Review from Unit 9: 也 comes before 常. The previous speaker has said they often watch movies.

u10-we-all-often.note: Each of us often watches movies. We may watch separately.

u10-they-all-exercise.note: 都 includes each person; 常 describes the frequency of exercise.

u10-they-tea-too.pinyin: Tāmen yě dōu cháng hē chá.
u10-they-tea-too.meaning: They all often drink tea too.
u10-they-tea-too.note: Context: I often drink tea. Build 喝茶 → 常喝茶 → 都常喝茶 → 也都常喝茶.

u10-we-swim-too.note: Context: you often swim. Add our whole group and the same habit.

u10-i-no-brother-either.meaning: I do not have an older brother either.
u10-i-no-brother-either.note: Context: another person has no older brother. 也 adds me to the same situation; 沒有 is the negative of 有.

u10-no-siblings.text: 我沒有哥哥，也沒有姐姐。
u10-no-siblings.pinyin: Wǒ méiyǒu gēge, yě méiyǒu jiějie.
u10-no-siblings.meaning: I do not have an older brother, and I do not have an older sister either.
u10-no-siblings.note: The second clause keeps talking about 我. Put 也 before the second 沒有.

u10-she-no-sister-either.meaning: She does not have an older sister either.
u10-she-no-sister-either.note: Context: I have no older sister. Her situation matches mine.

u10-review-not-often.meaning: I do not often watch movies.
u10-review-not-often.note: Review: 不常 is about frequency. It does not mean never, and it does not tell us whether I like movies.

u10-we-none-swim.note: Apply 不喜歡游泳 to each member of 我們: Person 1 ❌ · Person 2 ❌ · Person 3 ❌.

u10-they-none-coffee.pinyin: Tāmen dōu bù xǐhuān hē kāfēi.
u10-they-none-coffee.meaning: None of them likes drinking coffee.
u10-they-none-coffee.note: Everyone in 他們 has the negative preference. Use 都 before 不.

u10-we-none-brother.meaning: None of us has an older brother.
u10-we-none-brother.note: Here the set is 我們. Each member has no older brother.

u10-neither-sibling.meaning: Older brothers and older sisters — I have neither.
u10-neither-sibling.note: Here the set is 哥哥、姐姐, not a group of people who lack something. Topic-first structure is review; 都沒有 extends it to neither.

u10-they-not-all-swim.meaning: Not all of them like swimming.
u10-they-not-all-swim.note: Reject the claim that everyone likes swimming. The sentence gives no exact count.

u10-we-not-all-coffee.pinyin: Wǒmen bù dōu xǐhuān hē kāfēi.
u10-we-not-all-coffee.meaning: Not all of us like drinking coffee.
u10-we-not-all-coffee.note: At least one of us does not like drinking coffee. A mixed group is one possible situation.

u10-family-not-all-photos.pinyin: Wǒ jiārén bù dōu xǐhuān zhàoxiàng.
u10-family-not-all-photos.meaning: Not all my family members like taking photos.
u10-family-not-all-photos.note: The group is my family members. 不都 rejects the claim that every member likes taking photos.

u10-neither-sport.text: 打籃球、踢足球，我都不喜歡。
u10-neither-sport.pinyin: Dǎ lánqiú, tī zúqiú, wǒ dōu bù xǐhuān.
u10-neither-sport.meaning: Playing basketball and soccer — I like neither.
u10-neither-sport.note: The two activities are the topic set. 都 applies 不喜歡 to each activity. This reuses the topic structure from Unit 9 and 都不 from this unit.

u10-topic-photo.text: 這張照片，我覺得很好看。
u10-topic-photo.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhàopiàn, wǒ juéde hěn hǎokàn.
u10-topic-photo.meaning: As for this photo, I think it looks nice.
u10-topic-photo.note: Review: name the photo first, then comment on it. 這張照片 is one specific topic, so it does not by itself call for 都.

u10-two-tea-habits.text: 我常喝茶，我姐姐也常喝茶。
u10-two-tea-habits.pinyin: Wǒ cháng hē chá, wǒ jiějie yě cháng hē chá.
u10-two-tea-habits.meaning: I often drink tea; my older sister often drinks tea too.
u10-two-tea-habits.note: These are two matching habits. We can summarize the two people with 我們都常喝茶.

u10-we-all-tea.note: In the conversation, 我們 refers to my older sister and me. 都 includes both of us.

u10-common-dialogue.text: 你們都喜歡游泳嗎？我們不都喜歡游泳。
u10-common-dialogue.pinyin: Nǐmen dōu xǐhuān yóuyǒng ma? Wǒmen bù dōu xǐhuān yóuyǒng.
u10-common-dialogue.meaning: Do all of you like swimming? Not all of us like swimming.
u10-common-dialogue.note: The answer corrects the question’s all-person claim. This combines familiar 嗎 with the already-taught 不都; it introduces no new pattern.

u10-morning-tea.meaning: I often drink tea in the morning.
u10-morning-tea.note: 早上 sets the time; 常 stays before the action 喝茶.

u10-tomorrow-morning-swim.meaning: Tomorrow morning, we are going swimming.
u10-tomorrow-morning-swim.note: 明天 is the larger time and comes before 早上.

u10-also-all-morning.text: 他們也都喜歡早上游泳。
u10-also-all-morning.pinyin: Tāmen yě dōu xǐhuān zǎoshàng yóuyǒng.
u10-also-all-morning.meaning: They all also like swimming in the morning.
u10-also-all-morning.note: Context supplies another person who likes morning swimming. 也 adds the match; 都 includes all of 他們.

u10-evening-movie.meaning: I often watch movies in the evening.
u10-evening-movie.note: 晚上 comes before the habit 常看電影.

u10-tomorrow-evening-movie.meaning: We are watching a movie tomorrow evening.
u10-tomorrow-evening-movie.note: Use larger-to-smaller time order: 明天晚上.

u10-all-often-evening.pinyin: Wǒmen wǎnshàng dōu cháng kàn diànyǐng.
u10-all-often-evening.meaning: We all often watch movies in the evening.
u10-all-often-evening.note: 晚上 frames the habit; 都 includes everyone; 常 marks frequency.

u10-also-all-often-evening.text: 他們晚上也都常看電影。
u10-also-all-often-evening.pinyin: Tāmen wǎnshàng yě dōu cháng kàn diànyǐng.
u10-also-all-often-evening.meaning: They also all often watch movies in the evening.
u10-also-all-often-evening.note: After the time, build 也 + 都 + 常 + action in that order.

u10-dinner.meaning: I eat dinner in the evening.
u10-dinner.note: 吃 is the action and 晚飯 is the meal.

u10-dinner-together.note: 一起 comes before the action 吃晚飯.

u10-none-want-dinner.pinyin: Tāmen dōu bù xiǎng chī wǎnfàn.
u10-none-want-dinner.meaning: None of them wants to eat dinner.
u10-none-want-dinner.note: 都不 makes the negative apply to every person in 他們.

u10-not-all-want-dinner.pinyin: Tāmen bù dōu xiǎng chī wǎnfàn.
u10-not-all-want-dinner.meaning: Not all of them want to eat dinner.
u10-not-all-want-dinner.note: 不都 means the whole group does not share the statement; some still may want dinner.

u10-dinner-how-about.text: 我們晚上一起吃晚飯，好不好？
u10-dinner-how-about.pinyin: Wǒmen wǎnshàng yìqǐ chī wǎnfàn, hǎo bu hǎo?
u10-dinner-how-about.meaning: How about we eat dinner together this evening?
u10-dinner-how-about.note: The full plan comes first; 好不好 asks for agreement.

u10-swim-how-about.text: 我們明天早上去游泳，好不好？
u10-swim-how-about.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān zǎoshàng qù yóuyǒng, hǎo bu hǎo?
u10-swim-how-about.meaning: How about we go swimming tomorrow morning?
u10-swim-how-about.note: 明天早上 gives the time; 好不好 checks the suggestion.

u10-sister-morning.text: 我早上常喝茶，我姐姐早上也常喝茶。
u10-sister-morning.pinyin: Wǒ zǎoshàng cháng hē chá, wǒ jiějie zǎoshàng yě cháng hē chá.
u10-sister-morning.meaning: I often drink tea in the morning; my older sister also often drinks tea in the morning.
u10-sister-morning.note: The second 也常 marks a matching morning habit.

u10-we-all-morning-tea.pinyin: Wǒmen zǎoshàng dōu cháng hē chá.
u10-we-all-morning-tea.meaning: We all often drink tea in the morning.
u10-we-all-morning-tea.note: The shared habit is morning tea; 都 includes everyone and 常 marks frequency.

u10-eat-dishes.note: 菜 refers to the dishes, while 晚飯 names the evening meal.

u10-vietnam-food.meaning: I would like to eat Vietnamese food.
u10-vietnam-food.note: The country name 越南 modifies 菜.

u10-vietnam-evening.pinyin: Wǒmen wǎnshàng qù chī Yuènán cài.
u10-vietnam-evening.meaning: We are going to eat Vietnamese food this evening.
u10-vietnam-evening.note: Name the time before 去吃.

u10-vietnam-plan.text: 我們明天晚上一起去吃越南菜，好不好？
u10-vietnam-plan.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān wǎnshàng yìqǐ qù chī Yuènán cài, hǎo bu hǎo?
u10-vietnam-plan.meaning: How about we go eat Vietnamese food together tomorrow evening?
u10-vietnam-plan.note: A complete plan: people, time, together, activity, then an invitation to agree.

u10-none-vietnam.pinyin: Wǒmen dōu bù xiǎng chī Yuènán cài.
u10-none-vietnam.meaning: None of us wants to eat Vietnamese food.
u10-none-vietnam.note: 都不 says that every person has the negative preference.
